name: interchangeable_collapse
provenance: Adversarial fixture A19 'Interchangeable domains' (VS2-C audit D5). Two interchangeable normal domains d1 and d2 (both class 'fungible'), budget one unit of each, two Trials worth 5 and 3, every positive amount a legal entry, optional allocation. Each domain unit is placed on trial_a, trial_b, or left as residue, giving 3x3 = 9 legal allocations. Because d1 and d2 are interchangeable, allocations differing only by swapping the two domains have identical per-Trial totals and source counts and therefore collapse to one behavioural class: the domain-swap pairs {(1,0) via d1, (1,0) via d2}, {(0,1) via d1, (0,1) via d2}, and the two ways to make (1,1) each merge (size 2), while (0,0), both-on-trial_a (2,0) and both-on-trial_b (0,2) are singletons. Result: 9 legal, 6 collapsed classes, class sizes {1,1,1,2,2,2}. This is the only committed fixture whose collapse is a GENUINE strategic merge (collapsed < legal), so it is the only one that can catch a merge that fails to merge or merges wrongly (A15 tests inflation invariance only). The oracle is hand-derived in the audit, not reverse-engineered from engine output (REQ-9.4). Config lives in configs/toy/interchangeable_5_3.json.

expected.notes: 9 legal (3 placements per domain x 2 domains); 6 behavioural classes after collapsing the three interchangeable domain-swap pairs; class-size multiset {1,1,1,2,2,2}.
